title: Debito do CAM-424: passFloor exigido IGUAL a contagem corrente se auto-invalida a cada teste adicionado, ja ficou stale 3 vezes dentro do proprio PRD
description:
Debito preciso do ciclo do CAM-424, que terminou em MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT no round 3. NAO ha gate vermelho: a suite fecha 5734 pass / 0 fail e o gate de ratchet funciona. O debito e de fidelidade de registro mais uma armadilha estrutural que se repete sozinha.

ATENCAO DE PROCEDIMENTO, ler antes de agir: o array review.findings do prd.json do CAM-424 esta STALE. Ele carrega o texto do round 2 e afirma duas coisas que ja foram consertadas, entre elas que scripts/test-in-container.ts nao chama checkSuiteRan. FALSO no HEAD do branch: a chamada existe em scripts/test-in-container.ts:238, checkSuiteRan(output, containerExpectation.passFloor, 'container'), rodando ANTES da comparacao de skip. Esse WARNING do round 3 esta RESOLVIDO. E a segunda vez que este projeto observa o array review.findings mentir (a primeira foi registrada no journal do CAM-434). Re-rodar os oraculos e o unico caminho confiavel; nao filar nem planejar em cima daquele array.

DEBITO 1, imediato e medido. test/helpers/lane-expectations.json grava host.passFloor = 5731 enquanto a medicao real no HEAD do branch e 5734 pass / 0 fail (rodado a mao pelo orquestrador em 2026-07-28T00:42Z com o loop terminal e sem contencao: "Ran 5734 tests across 341 files", 134.20s). Stale por 3, que sao exatamente os 3 testes que a US-R2-002 adicionou. O campo host.measuredVia tambem afirma 5731 em prosa, ou seja o arquivo declarado pela AC1 da US-005 como "the durable record for the triage evidence" carrega uma alegacao que qualquer leitor falsifica com um comando. NAO MEDI a lane de container (exige Docker de pe): o valor gravado e 5691, medido pelo reviewer no round 2, e provavelmente esta stale pelos mesmos 3, mas isso e INFERENCIA e precisa ser medido antes de escrever qualquer numero novo. Nao copiar 5694 daqui.

DEBITO 2, a causa estrutural, e o motivo real desta issue existir. A AC5 da US-005 exige que "the host lane's recorded passFloor EQUALS the measured full-PATH pass count on this branch", justificando que "the lane file's own recorded values are the ONE place a frozen literal belongs". A carve-out esta meio certa: um piso precisa mesmo de referencia fixa, porque derivar o piso da rodada que se esta checando e vacuo. Mas exigir que o piso seja IGUAL a contagem corrente nao e piso, e asserção de igualdade com nome enganoso, e garante invalidacao a cada teste adicionado, nesta PRD e em TODA PRD futura.

EVIDENCIA CONCLUSIVA, tres invalidacoes dentro de UM PRD, com workers que estavam olhando para o arquivo:
  US-006     escreveu 5720
  US-R1-002  adicionou 11 testes  -> stale (pego no review round 2)
  US-R2-001  corrigiu para 5731
  US-R2-002  adicionou 3 testes   -> stale de novo (estado atual)
Duas rodadas de review inteiras foram gastas neste unico campo.

O CAMPO FAZ DOIS TRABALHOS E SO UM PRECISA DE PRECISAO: (a) limiar de gate, que so precisa ser um limite inferior generoso, porque um piso de 5000 pega uma rodada crashada exatamente tao bem quanto 5731 e nunca envelhece; e (b) registro documental da medicao exata, que ja tem campo proprio, o measuredVia, e que pode carregar data sem virar gate. Contraste deliberado: expectedSkips e outra historia e DEVE continuar exigindo igualdade exata, porque detectar drift de skip e o proposito inteiro do ratchet. A mudanca proposta e so no passFloor.

DIRECAO A VALIDAR NA SPEC, nao decidida: (a) relaxar a AC para piso generoso com folga declarada (por exemplo um piso que so falha quando a contagem cai abaixo de alguma margem do ultimo bom conhecido), mantendo a medicao exata datada no measuredVia; ou (b) manter igualdade e adicionar um gate que RECOMPUTA e falha quando o arquivo diverge, transformando a manutencao manual em erro deterministico em vez de dependencia de memoria humana. A opcao (b) e mais estrita porem paga o custo de rodar a suite duas vezes, o que ja e reclamacao aberta neste repo (CAM-423). Medir esse custo antes de escolher.

ORACULO, atencao a regra de especie (patterns.md): NAO escrever oraculo que congele 5734, 5731, 5691 nem nenhuma contagem citada aqui, porque a contagem sobe a cada ciclo e congelar reproduz exatamente o defeito que esta issue descreve. O pin de invariancia correto compara valor gravado contra valor DERIVADO em tempo de checagem. E o oraculo de deteccao precisa ser varrido VERMELHO contra o HEAD atual, onde o arquivo JA esta stale: se ficar verde contra o estado atual, esta quebrado.

spec.scope: Retire the self-invalidating maintenance of test/helpers/lane-expectations.json passFloor by making the gate that ALREADY measures enforce a declared minimum headroom, and re-record both lanes from real measurements taken on this branch. READ THIS FIRST, because measurement inverted the premise recorded in this issue's own description: the description assumes the defect is that an acceptance criterion 'demands passFloor EQUALS the current count'. Nothing in the tree enforces that. Measured on main at 3777652a on 2026-07-28: scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts:205 is 'if (observedPass === null || observedPass < passFloor)', i.e. a genuine lower bound; a stale-low floor PASSES the gate. Executed proof: checkSuiteRan(out, 5758, 'host') returns null (accepted) and checkSuiteRan(out, 5759, 'host') returns a failing result. The equality demand survived only as prose in a PRD that no longer exists on main (prd.json is dropped from main by the CAM-27 invariant), so there is nothing to relax and no gate to loosen. What IS live and defective: (1) the recorded host passFloor is 5731 while the branch measures 5758 pass / 0 fail across 343 files, the FOURTH invalidation and the first one across PRDs rather than inside one, caused by the 27 tests CAM-448 added with nobody touching the lane file; (2) the host measuredVia prose asserts '5731 pass / 0 fail', a claim any reader falsifies with one command, inside the file US-005 of CAM-424 declared to be the durable record of the triage evidence; (3) nothing prevents a future author from re-recording the floor at equality and restarting the churn. Option (b) from the description, keep equality and add a recompute-and-compare gate, is REJECTED on merits and not on cost: bun run check:all already invokes the full suite THREE times (scripts/check-all.ts:78 gate 'test', scripts/check-coverage.ts:131 spawnSync bun test --coverage, scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts:224 spawnSync bun test), which CAM-423 measured at 95.9 percent of spine cost, and CI adds a fourth in-container run; a recompute gate would buy a fifth full run to enforce an invariant that is not real. Measurement opened a third path that the description did not list and that dominates both: check-skip-ratchet.ts already runs the suite and already holds observedPass and passFloor in the same function, so enforcing headroom there costs ZERO additional suite runs and converts human-memory maintenance into a deterministic error, which is exactly what option (b) wanted and could not afford. IN SCOPE: the headroom rule, re-recording both lanes from real measurement, and writing the convention down so it cannot be re-invented. OUT OF SCOPE and explicitly preserved: expectedSkips strict two-directional equality, which is correct and whose entire purpose is drift detection.
acceptanceCriteria:
AC1 (species: change-DETECTING; SWEPT RED against main by execution on 2026-07-28). scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts exports a named, doc-commented constant MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM with a value of at least 50, and the suite-ran check REJECTS a lane whose recorded passFloor leaves less than that headroom below the observed pass count. The rejection message must name the too-tight-floor failure mode distinctly and must NOT reuse the existing crashed-run wording 'suite likely crashed or ran only a subset', because the two failure modes demand opposite operator responses (re-record the floor lower vs investigate a broken run). ORACLE, runs in milliseconds, no suite run: bun -e 'import { checkSuiteRan } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const out=" 5758 pass
 0 fail
Ran 5758 tests across 343 files. [1s]
"; const r=checkSuiteRan(out,5758,"host"); process.exit(r===null?1:0)'. This exits 1 on main today (the gate ACCEPTS a floor equal to the observed count, verified by running it) and must exit 0 after this story. NOTE ON LITERALS: the 5758 in this oracle is a fixture string handed to a pure function inside the oracle itself, it is self-contained and cannot rot. Do NOT write 5758, 5731, 5734 or 5691 into lane-expectations.json as a frozen comparand, into any gate, or into any test expectation; freezing a live-growing count is the exact defect this issue exists to remove.

AC2 (species: change-DETECTING; RED once AC1 lands, GREEN when this lands). Both lanes in test/helpers/lane-expectations.json are re-recorded from measurements taken on THIS branch, with each passFloor at least MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM below its freshly measured pass count, and measuredAt / measuredVia restated to describe that measurement with its date and the exact command used. No object in the file may state a pass number in prose that contradicts the number recorded in the same object. Measured baseline for the host lane on main 3777652a at 2026-07-28: 'Ran 5758 tests across 343 files' with 5758 pass / 0 fail in 135.83s; recorded floor 5731, so the live gap is 27 and any MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM of 50 or more makes main RED. Do not copy 5758 forward as the new floor: measure again on the branch and record a floor with real headroom. ORACLE: bun scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts exits 0. This oracle is honest only in this order, first AC1 makes it red, then AC2 makes it green; state that order in the handoff.

AC3 (species: invariance PIN; green by construction, comparand derived live). expectedSkips keeps strict two-directional equality and the headroom rule applies ONLY to passFloor. The doc comment at scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts explaining that any delta in either direction fails must survive in substance. These three tests must still exist and pass, each verified on main 2026-07-28 to match exactly 1 test with 1 pass / 0 fail. ORACLES, each must report a NONZERO pass count and 0 fail, and a run that matches 0 tests is a FAILURE and never a success: bun test -t 'delta fails and names the delta'; bun test -t 'a decrease also fails and names the negative delta'; bun test -t 'newly introduced skip on the host lane'.

AC4 (species: contradiction handling, mandatory because AC1 breaks a currently GREEN test). AC1 contradicts test/check-skip-ratchet.test.ts:86, whose full name is 'null (suite ran cleanly) when tally line present and pass count clears the floor': it feeds fixture passFloor 5700 against a fixture output of 5702 pass, a gap of 2, which the new headroom rule must reject. That test must be REPAIRED by giving its fixtures real headroom, and must SURVIVE under a name that still contains the substring 'pass count clears the floor'. It must NOT be deleted, and the contradiction must NOT be resolved by deletion. The same repair applies to test/test-in-container.test.ts:375 'exits 0 when the completion tally is present and observed pass meets the container passFloor' if its fixtures leave less than MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM. A NEW test must additionally pin the too-tight rejection under a stable, parenthesis-free name containing the substring 'floor too tight'. ORACLES, each must report a NONZERO pass count and 0 fail: bun test -t 'pass count clears the floor'; bun test -t 'observed pass meets the container passFloor'; bun test -t 'under-runs the recorded passFloor'; bun test -t 'floor too tight'. WARNING, verified the hard way while authoring this spec on 2026-07-28: bun test -t treats its argument as a REGEX, so the parentheses in the full test name above make it match 0 tests ('Searched 343 files, skipping 5758 tests'). Every -t oracle in this PRD uses a parenthesis-free substring for that reason; never reintroduce parentheses into one.

AC5 (species: invariance PIN, cost containment). The gate spine must NOT gain a fourth full-suite invocation, and no new gate is added to the check-all manifest. The headroom check MUST reuse the output that scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts already captures at line 224; it must not spawn a suite run of its own. Measured on main 2026-07-28: exactly 2 spawnSync bun-test call sites in scripts/ (check-coverage.ts:131 and check-skip-ratchet.ts:224) plus 1 declarative 'bun test' gate in scripts/check-all.ts:78, totalling 3. ORACLES: test "$(grep -rn "Bun.spawnSync(\['bun', 'test'" scripts/*.ts | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "2"; and bun test -t 'has 14 gates in order' must report a NONZERO pass count and 0 fail (test/check-all.test.ts:67 asserts the manifest has exactly 14 gates and names each one in order, so adding a gate would break it).

AC6 (species: change-DETECTING, honesty of the container lane). The container lane must be RE-MEASURED for real, never inferred and never derived from the host lane's delta; the issue description explicitly forbids copying a number here. Docker was verified UP on 2026-07-28 (Docker 29.4.0), so this is executable in-cycle. Update the container expectedSkips, passFloor and measuredVia from that actual run. If Docker is unavailable when the story runs, HALT and report the blocker rather than writing an inferred number: an invented container count reproduces the exact fidelity defect this issue exists to fix. ORACLE: bun scripts/test-in-container.ts exits 0.

AC7 (species: change-DETECTING, durable prevention; SWEPT RED against main on 2026-07-28). scripts/cam/patterns.md gains a bullet recording the convention so no future spec author re-invents the equality demand: passFloor is a floor carrying declared headroom and must never be maintained at equality with the current pass count, expectedSkips is the deliberate opposite and must stay exactly equal because detecting skip drift is the whole purpose of the ratchet, and the evidence is four measured invalidations (US-006 wrote 5720, US-R1-002 added 11 and staled it, US-R2-001 corrected to 5731, US-R2-002 added 3 and staled it again, then CAM-448 added 27 across PRDs and staled it a fourth time). ORACLE: grep -q 'never be maintained at equality' scripts/cam/patterns.md. Verified ABSENT on main today (grep -c returns 0), so this is red now and green when the bullet lands.
gotchas: bun test -t treats its argument as a REGEX, not a literal. A test name containing parentheses will match 0 tests and print 'matched 0 tests'. Every -t oracle here uses a parenthesis-free substring, and every -t oracle must require a NONZERO pass count, because a filter that matches zero tests must never read as success.

Do NOT freeze a live pass count as a comparand. 5758, 5734, 5731 and 5691 all appear in this spec as MEASURED EVIDENCE with a date, not as values to embed. Fixture literals passed to a pure function inside a self-contained oracle are fine; a recorded expectation compared against a growing suite is the defect itself.

No test loads the real test/helpers/lane-expectations.json from disk; both suites inject fakes (test/check-skip-ratchet.test.ts:158-169 uses passFloor 5700/5650, test/test-in-container.test.ts:41-52 defaults containerPassFloor to 0). Changing the recorded numbers therefore breaks no test, which is also why the staleness went undetected for four cycles. A container fixture floor of 0 makes any headroom check pass trivially, so the AC4 repair must give it a realistic fixture.

Both readers parse the lane file with an unchecked 'as LaneExpectationsFile' cast (scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts:230 and scripts/test-in-container.ts:288), and measuredAt, measuredVia and the entire triage block are never read by any code. Adding or restating those fields is safe but is also silently unvalidated; do not assume a typo would be caught.
bun run check:all already runs the full suite three times and CI adds a fourth in-container run. Any design that adds another full run is rejected by AC5.

Never read review findings from prd.json's review.findings array. That array has now lied three times in this project's history (CAM-434, CAM-424, CAM-448), carrying verbatim text from a previous round describing defects that were already fixed. The truth lives in scripts/cam/review-report.json under the key 'text', with review-artifact.txt as the artifact of record.
Scratch, backup and payload files must never be written inside the repo tree. Any untracked file anywhere in the working tree fails the plan preflight clean-tree guard. Use /tmp.

The installed binary and the running sidecar were rebuilt to 0.266.0 at the start of this cycle, so they carry the CAM-448 budget separation. If a plan escalates, the exhaustedBudget discriminator on the marker distinguishes a lint-budget exhaustion from an auditor-budget exhaustion.
domainTerms: passFloor: a per-lane LOWER BOUND on the pass count that a clean suite run must clear, carrying declared headroom below the current measured count. It is deliberately not a snapshot of the current count, and maintaining it at equality is the defect this issue removes.

MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM: the minimum gap that must separate a recorded passFloor from the observed pass count. Enforcing a minimum gap is anti-churn and self-satisfying over time, because adding tests only widens the gap; it fires once, is fixed once, and then stays satisfied unless someone re-tightens the floor toward equality.

expectedSkips: a per-lane EXACT skip count compared with strict two-directional equality, the deliberate opposite of passFloor, because detecting skip drift in either direction is the entire purpose of the ratchet.
lane: one of the two execution environments the suite runs in, host or container, each with independently measured expectations.
